newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar finds a few friends at close.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar finds a few friends at close.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar found a few friends at lower levels on Monday after largely stabilising in the aftermath of last week's easing by the Reserve Bank.
By the close the Kiwi was at 0.6779/86, not far adrift from its 0.6784/91 open, having traded a 0.6774-00 range.
The morning's March quarter GDP data came in well below market expectations and ensured that the kiwi lingered low in its day's range by reinforcing hopes for further easing.
The Trade-Weighted Index ended at 66.73 from its 66.89 open and the Reserve Bank's live nominal monetary conditions index was at 773.85, versus 788.57 this morning.
"It's trading at the bottom of the MCI band that the RBNZ outlined on Friday, so people are a bit reluctant to take it lower," said one dealer.
"It's probably more finding MCI support as opposed to support for the Kiwi in its own right," he said.
He expected offshore markets to set direction based on where the MCI is at any given time.
But dealers now expect the Kiwi now to be confined to a 0.6760-0.6810 range over the short term.
